about.title: Gustine Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Gustine is a small town, but its markets, restaurants along 4th Street and 6th Avenue, and rural properties near Rt 140 and Rt 33 still see their share of falls caused by wet floors, cracked walkways, poor lighting, or uneven parking lots. When a property owner or manager knew about a hazard — or reasonably should have — and didn't fix it or warn visitors, California law allows an injured person to pursue compensation. Because Gustine businesses are often smaller operations without dedicated security staff, hazards can go unaddressed for longer, and surveillance footage may be overwritten quickly if not requested right away. If you were hurt on someone else's property in Gustine, we can evaluate what happened and explain your options at no cost. There's no obligation, and we only get paid if you recover money.

items.title: Notice Requirement Guidance
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. We can help identify evidence, like prior complaints or repair records, that supports this.

items.title: Time-Sensitive Evidence Preservation
items.desc: Surveillance video at Gustine businesses is often deleted within days or weeks. Acting quickly can help preserve footage and other proof before it disappears.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced but not eliminated even if you were partly at fault. We can help present your side clearly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Gustine?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If a government entity owns the property, such as a city building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. It's best to speak with us as soon as possible to avoid missing a deadline.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for my fall?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, so being partly at fault doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your total recovery may simply be reduced by your share of responsibility. We can help explain how this might apply to your specific situation.

items.question: What should I do after a fall at a Gustine business or apartment?
items.answer: Try to document the hazard with photos, note the time and location, and ask if the property has surveillance cameras covering the area. Since many Gustine properties are smaller businesses, footage may not be preserved for long, so acting quickly matters. Reporting the incident to management and seeking medical attention can also help support your claim.
